subject: Residual token crediting and minimum-slab clarifications for pilot pricing
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acmeauto.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmeauto.com>
Date: 2027-03-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify how residual tokens & minimum slabs apply to our pilot

Hi Soojin / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Before we sign the pilot PO our procurement team wants one tight example they can include with the contract language:

- We plan to run 15k short requests/day for 30 days (avg prompt+response ~120 tokens).
- There are occasional long analysis runs (one-off) that hit ~8k tokens.

Questions:
1) How do you round or bucket tokens for small-volume calls — do you charge per-request rounded up to the nearest 32 tokens, 100 tokens, or per-token?
2) If a long 8k token call happens, how is that apportioned when we also have many small calls that day — does the long call consume our monthly committed units first, or is it billed separately?
3) If we don’t fully use the reserved slab (e.g., leftover 200k tokens at month end), do those tokens roll as residual credits? How are they represented on the invoice?

Procurement would like one sample invoice showing the month where we consumed 70% of the slab and had two long calls. Can you send a calculation and the sample invoice line items?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — our legal is on a short timeline.

Best,
Alex
Director of AI Products
Acme Automotive

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acmeauto.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-14T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify how residual tokens & minimum slabs apply to our pilot

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear ask. I pulled together a short worked example and a sample invoice stub (attached) — summary below, then I answered each question explicitly.

Summary (pilot month):
- Committed slab: 1,000,000 tokens / month (reserved capacity pilot)
- Actual consumption: 700,000 tokens consumed across short requests + 2 long calls (8k each)
- Invoice: charge for 700k tokens consumed from slab; because slab was not exceeded, no overage charge; leftover 300k tokens shown as "Committed credit balance" on invoice and available to roll into next month per pilot terms.

Answers:
1) Rounding/bucketing: We bill at per-token granularity for accuracy, but we apply a minimum per-request floor of 64 tokens for streaming/short-call efficiency. That means any request that is <64 tokens will be billed as 64. We do not round up to a large quantum like 100 unless you opt into a bundled floor.
2) Long calls & allocation: Consumption is deducted from the committed slab first (FIFO within month). If a long call causes you to exceed the slab, the overage is billed at the agreed overage rate and shows as a separate line item. We do support configurable per-route caps to prevent a single long call from exhausting the slab — we can set a per-call soft cap and route long jobs to a dedicated burst pool (if you want isolation).
3) Residuals: For pilot customers, leftover tokens are represented on the invoice as a residual credit line ("Committed credit balance") and are available to apply to the following month's consumption. If you convert to an annual commit, we can also offer true roll-forward credits for up to 3 months; otherwise pilot credits expire after 30 days.

Attached: token_calc_example.xlsx (worked calculations) and sample_invoice.pdf.

Next steps: If you want, I can produce two sample invoice PDFs — one where we hit 70% usage and another where you exceed the slab by 10% (to show overage math). Which do you prefer?

Thanks,
Soojin
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-15T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: pilot concession and packaging suggestion (FYI)

Looping in for context. A few negotiation points I recommend if Acme pushes for lower effective unit price: 

- Offer a one-month 10% pilot discount on consumed tokens (not on committed slab) in exchange for a case study and 30-day tech review.
- Add an explicit per-call soft cap of 10k tokens for the pilot to limit blast risk; long analytical jobs can be routed as "batch-analytics" with separate pricing if they exceed that.
- Represent residuals as a distinct invoice line and allow a one-time manual rollover for pilot customers rather than automatic multi-month roll-forwards.

Ben — can you check the sample calc in the attachment and confirm the invoice line naming matches finance templates?

Marissa
Head of Sales Ops

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-15T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: pilot concession and packaging suggestion (FYI)

On the calc: numbers look clean. A couple small edits for invoicing language:
- Show "Committed slab (tokens)" and "Consumed tokens" as separate lines; include a third line "Residual credit" with negative amount that reduces total due.
- If we give a 10% pilot discount, list it as a separate discount line so accounting can reconcile it to AR.

I'll update the sample_invoice.pdf and return to Soojin.

—Ben
Senior Finance Manager

Alex — attached is the updated sample invoice showing the 70% consumption case and the overage scenario (PDFs). Key points reflected:

- Line items: Committed slab, Consumed tokens, Residual credit (negative), Pilot discount (10% on consumed tokens), Overage (if any).
- Per-request floor: 64 tokens as discussed.
- Long-call protection: we added a per-call soft cap at 10k tokens for the pilot; any job >10k triggers an alert and needs approval to route to burst pool.

If that looks good, I can generate a short amendment to the SOW with the billing table (one paragraph) and send the DocuSign link. For timing, we can turn the pilot on within 7 business days of the signed amendment.
